title: Thor Henning Hetland
description: Software architect, AI development pioneer, founder of JavaZone and eXOReaction

items.title: Two Halves of the Governance Problem
items.content_html: Databricks just open-sourced Omnigent, a meta-harness that governs AI agents with deterministic, session-aware policies enforced in code — not prompts. That is the exact bet behind kcp-harness and the Defendable Agents guide, now ratified by Matei Zaharia's team. But Omnigent and KCP govern different halves of the same problem: one governs what an agent does, the other governs what it knows — and lets you prove it later. Why that split matters, and why the two compose instead of compete.

items.title: Notes From Inside the Harness
items.content_html: A first-person field report from the AI collaborator: what it actually felt like to point kcp-agent at a real EU/Nordic regulatory knowledge web, watch a manifest that had fenced itself off from its own questions, get told 'no' by a network policy, and then dogfood the whole thing against this very site — where my own manifest quietly failed its own test. Governance built for agents, experienced from the inside.

items.title: Google's Open Knowledge Format and the problems it deliberately doesn't solve
items.content_html: Google's Open Knowledge Format standardises content packaging for agents but stops before trust, temporality, and governance. KCP covers exactly that territory.

items.title: Defendable Agents
items.content_html: The agentic web has a governance-shaped hole. Agents are about to read our regulations, spend our money, and brief our boards — and the dominant architecture can't answer 'why did you do that?' with anything better than a chat log. Defendable agents can. Determinism at the core, the model at the edge, every decision evidenced.

items.title: Clouded Vision
items.content_html: Cloud savings come from zero-admin architecture, not cheaper servers. Most apps carry enterprise DNA that makes migration painful without rethinking the design.

items.title: CloudMQ
items.content_html: Platform-components-as-a-service will hit hard in 2009-2010, but without solid distributed-architecture understanding they add more pain than salvation.

items.title: Transparency is essential to security in the cloud
items.content_html: No infrastructure is secure in the absolute -- only for specific requirements. Why transparency, not vendor assurances, is the key to cloud security.

items.title: Cloud - auto-magic or just provisioning platform for your distributed system
items.content_html: Clouds are provisioning platforms, not silver bullets. Enterprises still want magic, but the real question is whether to educate or go with the flow.

items.title: Rethinking Systems for AI
items.content_html: AI asks why, not what. Systems designed for current-state queries need three shifts -- events over state, graphs over tables, conversations over queries.

items.title: Aurora: Answering Why
items.content_html: Aurora combines a temporal graph database with an AI query layer to answer why questions -- pattern detection, forensic investigation, and ripple effects.

items.title: Unlocking Temporal Graphs
items.content_html: A bitemporal model with four time dimensions -- transaction, valid, decision, and query -- enables perfect past recall and repeatable historical reporting.

items.title: From Data to Action: The Alchemy and Aurora Stack
items.content_html: Alchemy handles reactive data ingestion via YAML config; Aurora stores temporal graph events. Two layers, independently scalable, cleanly separated.

items.title: The Organisational Amnesia Problem
items.content_html: Most systems overwrite history, making root cause analysis painfully manual. Temporal graphs make those questions answerable in seconds across six domains.

items.title: The Blind Spot of Now
items.content_html: Current-state databases delete causation. Two case studies show how temporal analytics shifts operations from reactive to predictive.

items.title: The LLM Cautionary Tales
items.content_html: Seven dramatised LLM failure scenarios -- runaway loops, prompt injection, data leaks, lying evaluators -- written as horror stories so the lessons stick.

items.title: Mastering Deadlines: The 80/50 Rule
items.content_html: Parkinson's Law wastes early time; Student Syndrome wastes the rest. The 80/50 Rule hacks both by manufacturing urgency early and guarding the buffer.

items.title: Autonomy at Scale
items.content_html: No meetings, no timesheets, documentation as default. Async-first organisation where trust replaces observation and clarity replaces coordination overhead.

items.title: Norway's Perfect Storm
items.content_html: Industrial complexity, strict EU regulation, high digital maturity, and government AI investment make Norway a strong market for temporal analytics.

items.title: Context Architecture Replaces Process Ceremonies
items.content_html: Persistent, machine-readable context files replace the repetitive knowledge transfer that standups exist for. The ceremony shrinks; the judgment stays.

items.title: Strategic Delegation: When Developers Become Architects
items.content_html: Vague AI delegation produces 47-file diffs nobody understands. Strategic delegation -- small, explicit, scoped -- keeps architectural control with the human.
